text:
Sam (PM): Heads-up — Sales flagged a NimbusPay SLA problem. Customer reports a throughput/p95 spike after the routing change this morning. Alex pasted their notes below. Need to decide: hotfix vs. product work.

Alex (Sales): NimbusPay saw ~3x p95 increase for embeddings/chat calls starting ~06:10 UTC when we rolled the 'cost-optimized' routing policy. They're on Dedicated with a routing override. They say latency breaches are impacting their customers and may throttle traffic if not resolved. I collected traces and request IDs: https://redwood.atlassian.net/secure/attachments/nimbus-traces (redacted).

Maya (Eng): Reproduced locally using a traffic replay. New routing weights send many short requests to a lower-throughput pool which queues under burst. Root cause looks like: routing weight change + an autoscaler eviction during a noisy-neighbor period. Quick options: 1) pin NimbusPay to the stable pool, 2) rollback the routing change.

Aisha (SRE): Dashboards show CPU steal and queue length spike on pool-7 at 06:09. Autoscaler removed one 8x GPU instance right before the spike. We can pin route to stable pool, but that's a cost hit for the customer. Suggest hotfix to pin route + a product fix for routing safety.

Sam (PM): Tradeoff decision needed. Hotfix (1 day) to pin routing or rollback the policy; or full product fix (routing safety + headroom) which needs design and dev time. What does product fix look like and what's the launch criteria?

Maya (Eng): Proposed product fix scope: 1) route-level customer pinning API and override, 2) autoscaler safety margin for priority customers, 3) workload test harness that simulates bursts to verify p95 under autoscale events. Acceptance criteria: reproducible test harness, p95 within SLA (target: 99th <200ms for embeddings under standard load), rollout flag + canary, docs. Rough estimate: 3 sprints (~6 weeks) for full implementation; hotfix ~1-2 days to implement and push.

Alex (Sales): :warning: NimbusPay needs short-term assurance. They want hotfix + clear timeline for the permanent fix. I can push for a 2-week commitment if engineering can provide a concrete plan.

Sam (PM): OK — prioritize hotfix now. Create a product ticket for the permanent fix and surface on the roadmap as "Routing safety for priority customers." We'll treat any enterprise account with committed SLAs as P0. Maya/Aisha — can you draft a short tech spec and rollout plan by EOD?

Maya (Eng): On it. I'll draft the spec and post in #eng-architecture with sections: API surface, autoscaler changes, testing plan, and migration path. Will include acceptance criteria and a suggested rollout strategy. ETA EOD.

Aisha (SRE): I'll implement a temporary autoscaler guard to avoid scaling below 2 instances for that pool during high-priority windows and add a routing override for NimbusPay. I'll monitor metrics and set alert thresholds.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Autoscaler guard patch deployed to staging at 1918002234, promoted to canary at 1918003634.

Alex (Sales): I'll notify NimbusPay: hotfix is in flight, we're monitoring, and we'll provide a timeline for the permanent fix (est 6 weeks). I'll offer credits for the disruption.

Sam (PM): Action items recap: 1) Maya: tech spec + Jira ticket; 2) Aisha: apply hotfix + monitoring + temporary routing override; 3) Alex: customer comms. Reconvene tomorrow 10:00 UTC to review. Marking this P0 for SLA customers. :thumbsup:
